title: Ford’s Carhartt Package Expands to F-150 for 2027

body_markdown:
When automakers[collaborate](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/star-crossed-automotive-collaborations/) with non-automotive brands, the result doesn’t always make complete sense to the layman. A Carhartt edition Ford F-150, though? That is entirely natural.


The Carhartt package will be available on the F-150 for 2027, alongside[the previously announced Super Duty Carhartt](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/2027-ford-super-duty-carhartt-package-is-a-tasteful-nod-to-workwear/) . The package costs the same on the half-ton as it does on the three-quarter ton truck—$4195—and includes a very similar suite of aesthetic and practical upgrades.


Like the Super Duty Carhartt, the F-150 Carhartt is based on the 4×4-equipped XLT model. Along with regular XLT models, it wears an updated grille for 2027. Grayscale graphics on the tailgate and lower rockers proclaim its Carhartt-ization, plus a little white-and-yellow logo on the front fenders. A set of 20-inch wheels (the regular XLT 4×4 comes with 18s) with a six-spoke design unique to this package finishes things off. We appreciate that the visual theme of these wheels is obviously different than the rims on the Super Duty Carhartt, inspired, in part, by manhole covers. The decision on Ford’s part helps the two trucks feel more distinct, and less like the result of copy-pasting the same list of upgrades.

In keeping with Ford’s and Carhartt’s hard-working images, the F-150 Carhartt comes with a spray-in bedliner with “Carhartt” detailed on the inside of the tailgate. A dual exhaust and off-road running boards, while not carrying any Carhartt logos, gesture to the truck’s off-road capability. The interior features Carhartt-branded all-weather floor mats, only appropriate for vehicles that will almost certainly be used as daily drivers and subject to all manner of muddy, dirty, sandy, chalky, and salty footwear.

This is a pre-production model, so we hope that these wobbles will be worked out by the time production of customer models starts.


Ford


The seats are upholstered in a two-tone material that evokes Carhartt’s signature duck canvas jackets and bibs. (The two-tone look sets the F-150 Carhartt apart from the equivalent Super Duty, which uses a single, gray colorway.) They bear the Carhartt logos you’d expect, stitched into the headrests, but there’s more: Keen-eyed viewers will spot the line of triple stitching on the upper and lower sections of the seats and on the door cards, another detail shared with Carhartt workwear.


Ford


The F-150 Carhartt will start at $62,660 plus destination and delivery. (As of this writing, destination is $2795 for a 2026 F-150 XLT 4×4.) As with all other 2027 F-150s, the Carhartt edition trucks will come standard with a 3.0-liter, rather than the 2026’s 2.7-liter, EcoBoost V-6, and trucks equipped with BlueCruise will boast the ability to tow with the hands-free driver-assist system active, on pre-qualified roads.


The 2027 F-150 Carhartt is available for delivery now, and we fully expect this accessible, fashionable add-on to be a hit.
